skill.name: nansen-mpp-payment
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pay-per-call Nansen API access using the Tempo MPP CLI.
skill.summary: Use Tempo MPP to call paid Nansen API endpoints without an API key or local wallet setup.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but it instructs users to install Tempo with a remote installer and run wallet and paid API operations. Most markdown backtick detections are harmless formatting, but the pipe-to-shell installer, broad CLI permissions, and billable payment flow require remediation.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash installation with a verified package-manager path, checksum validation, and explicit user confirmation before execution.
Narrow allowed-tools to the exact Tempo and Nansen subcommands required, or require confirmation for wallet and paid request commands.
Add clear consent gates before wallet funding and paid API calls, including expected cost and endpoint target.
Document trusted domains and require users to verify endpoint URLs before sending requests.

content.user_title: Run Nansen API Calls Through Tempo MPP
content.value_statement: Paid Nansen API access can require API keys or wallet setup. This skill shows how to use Tempo MPP for pay-per-call requests.
actual_capabilities: Explain when Tempo MPP is the right Nansen access method.
List one-time Tempo CLI setup steps for wallet login and funding.
Show paid Nansen API request patterns using tempo request.
Help discover paid endpoint metadata through the Nansen well-known endpoint.
Compare MPP headers and wallet handling with x402.
limitations: Requires the Tempo CLI to be installed separately.
Does not manage API keys, wallet keys, or Nansen credentials.
Can trigger paid API requests when commands are executed.
Depends on Nansen and Tempo endpoint availability.

use_cases.title: Access Nansen Without API Keys
use_cases.description: Use Tempo MPP when a paid endpoint supports payment credentials and the user wants no long-lived API key.

use_cases.title: Test MPP Payment Flows
use_cases.description: Compare Nansen API key, x402, and MPP paths before building payment-aware API integrations.

use_cases.title: Document Paid Endpoint Discovery
use_cases.description: Check Nansen paid resource metadata and explain which payment rails are available for each endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Access Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner comparison of Nansen payment options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether Tempo MPP fits my Nansen task. I do not have a Nansen API key and want to avoid local wallet management.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Tempo Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Walk me through preparing Tempo for Nansen MPP access. Include login, funding checks, and approval points before paid requests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Paid Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a Nansen MPP request for this endpoint: [endpoint]. Include schema lookup, cost awareness, and required approvals.

prompt_templates.title: Review Payment Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Nansen workflow for API key, x402, and Tempo MPP tradeoffs: [workflow]. Identify payment, credential, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need to call a paid Nansen endpoint without an API key.
output: Use Tempo MPP only if the endpoint supports payment credentials.
Confirm wallet login and funding before any paid request.
Treat each request as billable and require explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Compare MPP with x402 for my Nansen workflow.
output_examples.output: MPP uses Tempo-managed payment credentials. x402 uses the Nansen CLI wallet flow. Choose based on wallet ownership and approval requirements.

output_examples.input: Can I discover which paid endpoints are available?
output_examples.output: Yes. Start with public endpoint metadata, then verify the target endpoint and payment rail before sending paid requests.

best_practices: Confirm user approval before installing Tempo or running billable requests.
Check endpoint schemas before sending paid requests.
Use read-only discovery steps before wallet funding or paid calls.
anti_patterns: Do not run remote installer scripts without verifying the source.
Do not send wallet or payment actions without explicit consent.
Do not use this skill when an API key or x402 flow is required.

faq.question: Does this skill install Tempo for me?
faq.answer: No. It documents the setup and expects separate installation with user approval.

faq.question: Can it call Nansen without an API key?
faq.answer: Yes, when the endpoint supports MPP and the user approves the paid request.

faq.question: Does it manage wallet keys?
faq.answer: No. Tempo manages the payment flow separately from the Nansen CLI wallet flow.

faq.question: Are requests free?
faq.answer: No. The documented API calls can be paid requests and should require explicit approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace x402?
faq.answer: No. It covers the MPP payment rail and explains when x402 remains the better choice.
